cohort: The study included 90 patients (54 male, 36 female) with Prader-Willi syndrome, whose data were collected from case records and retrospective birth questionnaires between 1991 and 2015.
finding: Neonatal hypotonia, reduced fetal movements, feeding difficulties, and cryptorchidism are key features that should immediately suggest Prader-Willi syndrome, aiding early diagnosis.
mod_finding: Breech presentation was reported in 23% of patients with Prader-Willi syndrome.
birth_weight: 24% of the patients had a birthweight <2500g.
gest_age: 26% of the patients were born preterm.
